name: Cambridge House, Auberge Collection
insider_take: Where 200 years of Mayfair grandeur meets the effortless intimacy of Auberge — Cambridge House isn't just a hotel, it's a piece of living London history on one of the world's most iconic streets.
whats_special: This breathtaking Grade I listed Georgian mansion on Piccadilly once served as the private residence of Lord Palmerston, the 19th-century British Prime Minister. Auberge Collection has masterfully transformed it into London's most talked-about luxury retreat, preserving original architectural details — soaring ceilings, marble fireplaces, and grand staircases — while layering in warm, residential sophistication. With just 102 Rooms & Suites, it delivers rare intimacy for a Mayfair address.
pro_tip: Request a room overlooking Piccadilly for a front-row seat to one of London's most storied streets, then walk directly across to Green Park for a morning stroll before the city wakes up.
dont_miss: Dine at the hotel's celebrated restaurant showcasing modern British cuisine, and make time to explore the immediate neighborhood — the Royal Academy of Arts, Bond Street's flagship boutiques, and the hidden arcades of Burlington and Piccadilly are all within a leisurely five-minute walk.
pros: Iconic Georgian Mayfair townhouse with stunning historic architecture and refined interiors
Prime Mayfair address steps from Piccadilly, Hyde Park, and London's finest shopping and dining
Intimate boutique atmosphere with highly personalized Auberge Collection service
World-class dining and cocktail experience anchored by celebrated culinary programming
Beautifully appointed guest rooms blending contemporary luxury with timeless British elegance
cons: Limited number of rooms means availability can be scarce, especially during peak London seasons
Premium Mayfair location comes with a luxury price point
